stories.headline: India offers 3-part plan to de-escalate Ukraine war
stories.title: India offers 3-part plan to de-escalate Ukraine war
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: India's proposal calls for a halt to attacks on energy facilities and critical infrastructure; measures to keep grain and energy shipments moving through Black Sea ports; and an end to strikes on merchant vessels, civilian crew and maritime trade routes.
The Indian proposals may not deal with the core demands of the war but deals with the critical question of economic security.

While attacks by Ukraine on Russian energy infrastructure has impacted global energy flows, Kiev has requested New Delhi to use its good offices with Russia enabling grain exports by Ukraine through Black Sea Ports, it has been learnt.
Attacks on merchant vessels in Black Sea have taken a toll on Indian seafarers and New Delhi had raised the issue with both Moscow and Kiev, officials here informed.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday called Prime Minister Narendra Modi to share his perspective on recent developments regarding the conflict.
Modi, on his part, conveyed India's readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at a peaceful resolution of the conflict.

stories.headline: Cyclone-hit villages in Prakasam district remain without electricity
stories.title: Cyclone-hit villages in Prakasam district remain without electricity
stories.summary: The villagers are going to the nearest urban centre to charge their mobile phones at a cost of ₹10 per charge and are facing difficulties in meeting their daily needs, including access to drinking water and arranging fuel for generators, sources say
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Since Cyclone Murasu hit the coastline of Andhra Pradesh, several villages in Nagulappalapadu, Kanigiri, Kothapatnam, Singarayakonda, and Addanki mandals of Prakasam district have been facing continuous power outages.

Though the Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited (APCPDCL) staff are undertaking restoration works on war-footing basis, the residents in these coastal villages are spending their nights by using oil lamps and candles.
According to source, the villagers are going to the nearest urban centre to charge their mobile phones at a cost of ₹10 per charge.
They are facing difficulties in meeting their daily needs, including access to drinking water and arranging fuel for generators.
Speaking to The Hindu, Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar said, “Initially, we have estimated an overall expenditure of ₹500 crore to repair the electric infrastructure damaged by the cyclone.
But, the budget has now crossed ₹700 crore to restore 35,000 poles across the State.”
Speaking about the restoration works in the villages of Prakasam district, he said, the APCPDCL officials are taking swift action to resolve the issues.
“The domestic power supply will be rectified in a day, and it will take three days to restore agricultural and aquaculture connections”.

APCPDCL (Projects & HRD) Director T.V.S.N. Murthy supervised the repair works on the 11 kV Ammanabrolu–Chavatapalem feeder—which had experienced a power interruption—directly at the site within the Naguluppalapadu section.
Additionally, he inspected the breakdown repair works being carried out on the 11 kV Chadalavada feeder in the same section.
He instructed the officials to expedite power restoration efforts and ensure that staff work in coordination to restore electricity supply as quickly as possible.
